priceSnapshot.source: OKX Public API v5 (market/ticker), fetched via in-page fetch() from the okx.com origin using Claude in Chrome (WebFetch through the sandbox proxy returned a stale cached snapshot ~5h old for OKX endpoints this run -- discarded per the freshness guard; browser in-page fetch used throughout for price, candles, open interest, funding, long/short ratio, and liquidation orders).
priceSnapshot.note: Since yesterday's midday report (84,178.6), the range top finally cracked: a confirmed 1H close at 84,724 (05:00 COT) broke the prior addIf (84,628.2), and price wicked to a fresh high of 85,258.8, but the breakout failed to extend and faded back under 84,000. Now at 83,963.3, roughly flat vs. the OKX 24h open (-0.64%), sitting closer to the defended support than the twice-rejected resistance.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close back below 82,874.5 (unbroken this session; low was 83,174.7) would signal the recovery attempt failed and downside continuation is resuming.

addIf.confirmation: Raised from 84,628.2 after that level saw one confirmed 1H close above it (84,724 at 05:00 COT) that failed to extend. A settled 1H close above 84,944.4 -- which has now capped two separate attempts (the 84,724 close and the 85,258.8 wick) -- would confirm the range top is actually breaking, not just testing.

decisionBox.changed: The old addIf (84,628.2) fired once on a settled 1H close (84,724, 05:00 COT) but the move immediately rolled back without building a higher low above it, even after wicking to a new high (85,258.8). Raising the bar to 84,944.4 -- the level that has now rejected both attempts -- rather than treating the single close as a resolved breakout. reduceIf/support unchanged and untested this session.
